items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I had people in it like Cozy Cole, Big Sid Catlett, Dickie Wells, Chu Chew Berry.

ctx.x: I had people in it like Cozy Cole, Big Sid Catlett, Dickie Wells, Chu Chew Berry.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Or even a Cozy Cole, you know, whom, of course, I’d probably get him to lighten up on the bass drum, you know.

ctx.x: Well, I think by 1933 the band was already working and recording, and I think this rehearsal period may have been that earlier stage in ’32.

Before, huh? It may have been, yeah. Cozy Cole, and at one point Sid Catlett. The only reason that I’m saying it . . . it seems that Teddy Wilson couldn’t have been in that rehearsal band, because he didn’t come to New York until 1933.
Right. By the time you went to get him, I think it was with actual engagements in mind.

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Benny Carter was in the band then with Willie Bryant, Benny Carter, Teddy Wilson.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, yeah, Benny Carter can tell you the same thing about that era. And well, see on a Sunday night

I think it was when the Band Box or the Rhythm Club would really jump. Because all the bands used to come up there and eat and sit down and play or listen to different musicians play and the reason I mention Sunday night because that would be the night that there would be a breakfast dance at Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson's band was there, and there was a great drummer in that band, his name is George Stafford.
